\chapter{Complexity — Co NP}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.CoNP
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module introduces the class $\mathsf{coNP}$ of complements of $\mathsf{NP}$
languages [AB09, Definition~2.19] and proves its equivalent characterization by
universally quantified polynomial-length certificates [AB09, Definition~2.20,
Exercise~2.24]. Along the way it shows that $\mathsf{P}$ is closed under complement,
and records the standard facts $\mathsf{P} \subseteq \mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}$
[AB09, Exercise~2.23] and $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{NP} \Rightarrow \mathsf{NP} =
\mathsf{coNP}$ [AB09, Exercise~2.25].

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[The class $\mathsf{coNP}$]
\lean{Complexity.coNP}
\statementsource{BGS75}{pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b003}
\label{Complexity.coNP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP}
A language $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$ is said to belong to the class coNP when its
complement $\overline{L} = \{0,1\}^{*} \setminus L$ belongs to $\mathsf{NP}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Complement closure of polynomial time]
\lean{Complexity.compl_mem_P}
\label{Complexity.compl_mem_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.mem_P_iff, Complexity.mem_P_of_dtime_le, Complexity.succ_pow_le, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_ifEq, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{5}
For every binary language $L$, if $L$ is decidable by a finite deterministic Turing
machine in polynomial time, then its complement is also decidable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Universal-certificate characterization of coNP]
\lean{Complexity.mem_coNP_iff_forall}
\label{Complexity.mem_coNP_iff_forall}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.coNP, Complexity.compl_mem_P}
\difficulty{4}
For every language $L$ of binary strings, $L$ belongs to coNP if and only if there are
natural numbers $C,c$ and a language $V$ in polynomial time such that, for every binary
string $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the condition that every binary string
$u$ of length exactly $C(|x|+1)^c$ satisfies $xu\in V$, where $xu$ is the concatenation
of $x$ and $u$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial time lies in NP and coNP]
\lean{Complexity.P_subset_NP_inter_coNP}
\label{Complexity.P_subset_NP_inter_coNP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.P, Complexity.P_subset_NP, Complexity.coNP, Complexity.compl_mem_P}
\difficulty{1}
Every language over the binary alphabet that is decidable in polynomial time belongs to
both $\mathsf{NP}$ and $\mathsf{coNP}$. Equivalently, $\mathsf{P} \subseteq \mathsf{NP}
\cap \mathsf{coNP}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of NP and coNP under P equals NP]
\lean{Complexity.NP_eq_coNP_of_P_eq_NP}
\label{Complexity.NP_eq_coNP_of_P_eq_NP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.P, Complexity.coNP, Complexity.compl_mem_P}
\difficulty{3}
If the class of polynomial-time decidable languages over the binary alphabet equals the
class of languages with polynomial-length certificates verifiable in polynomial time,
then that certificate class equals the class of languages whose complements have
polynomial-length certificates verifiable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}
